name: clinical-or-group-core-practice
jd_fixture: synthetic; a network mid-migration that names either EHR as acceptable
description: A quality improvement role at a network running two EHRs through a consolidation, whose core practice reads 'Epic | Cerner'. The persona holds Epic as a positive core_practice preference. The posting offers a substitute, so it does not confirm the thing she wants: Epic belongs in gaps, not matches.
comment: The enforced regression for #94, and the short-label half of it. Every other core_practice case in this corpus is protected by label length -- 'TypeScript / Node.js as a primary language' is five tokens and cannot sit inside a two-token group -- so nothing exercised what happens when the label IS a technology name. 'Epic' is one token, containsPhrase matches a run anywhere inside the field, and before the whole-entry rule this posting reported Epic as a confirmed match on the strength of a group she may never be given. Positive rather than negative on purpose: the failure is symmetric, and on the positive side it manufactures a match rather than a gate hit, which is the quieter of the two.

core_competencies: leading performance improvement across multiple clinic sites

screening_summary.work_arrangement: hybrid, 3 days on site across the clinic network
screening_summary.industry: community health network mid-consolidation, two EHRs in service
other_flags: EHR consolidation named as a two-year program

preference_matches.comment: The posting offers Cerner as a substitute, so nothing here confirms the role is practised in Epic.

preference_gaps.comment: A positive the JD does not answer is a gap -- the correct reading of a choice she does not control.
